statement: Run the entry gate and fix the body strike at the moment the short legs are sold; buy the wings in that same minute, after the body is chosen.
test: A fly ends up with uneven wings or an off-center body, or the gate result changes between the wing and body orders.

note: Wings for a 23 body were bought 3 minutes early; FLY bounced 23.19 -> 23.44, the body moved to 23.5 and the wings came out 3.5 / 4.5 wide.
Gate read at 11:38 PT (-6.4%); the stock later printed 12.05 (-7.2%), past the 7% skip line.

statement: Size by names, not contracts: 1 contract per earnings name during the data phase. Do not open 2 and trim later.
test: A position opened above 1 contract has to be trimmed to fit another passing name.

note: Opened 2, trimmed to 1 for FLY 12 minutes later: cost $10.32.

statement: Legging in with single-leg limits (wings first, then both shorts in one sitting, start at mid, one tick at a time) gets at least 95% of the fly's mid credit.
test: Entry fill_vs_mid below 0.95 on a chain with ATM spread under 25%.

note: 1.28 vs 1.325 mid = 0.966, but the short call needed the bid after 3 reprices in a falling tape.
2.65 vs 2.725 mid = 0.972 on a nickel-tick chain with a 16.7% ATM spread.

statement: A partial close is journaled as a heal with as_event qty_adjust, never exit_filled; after every journal write, check that the engine's open positions match the broker.
test: The engine's open_state or closed_trades disagrees with the broker after a journal write.

note: The trim was first written as exit_filled, which would have paired with the entry and lost the real exit; caught and corrected the same hour.

statement: Read the contract's tick size before pricing; nickel-tick chains need limits in $0.05 steps.
test: An order is rejected or mispriced because of tick size.

note: FLY trades in $0.05 ticks below $3; caught from get_option_instruments before the first order.

statement: When the broker rejects an order type, test the alternative with the cheapest possible leg before committing size.
test: A workaround is used at full size without a cheap test and fails part-way.

note: Multi-leg orders were blocked; a $4 long put showed single legs need no approval and that a held wing margins the short as a spread.

statement: Score skipped and rule-blocked names from option price history, not from an estimate of the next-day stock move.
test: A price-history score and an eyeball estimate agree in sign for 9 of 10 names.

note: The 11/06 scorecard said ALB would have been a small win (+$50 to +$120); the replay says a loss (-$20 to -$136).

statement: Monitoring cadence follows risk: poll every 10 minutes by default, every 3 minutes only near a breakeven, on expiration day, or while an exit is being worked.
test: A trigger is missed, or seen more than 10 minutes late, because of the slower cadence.

note: Three daemons at 3 minutes used about 475k tokens in one afternoon and raised one borderline alert.

statement: With wings one straddle-width out, the fly keeps about 70% of the straddle premium and wins when the move comes in under about 0.7 of the implied move.
test: More than 1 scored fly in 5 lands on the wrong side of the 0.7 line.

statement: The intraday-move gate (skip above 5%, or 7% with a sector move) does not improve results per trade.
test: Names blocked only by this gate do worse, as a share of max loss, than names that pass it. Evidence unit: one blocked name; supports = it would have won.

statement: For narrow-wing flies the sell threshold should tighten from edge ratio 0.85 to about 0.70, or the wings should widen.
test: Names with edge ratio between 0.70 and 0.85 average a positive result as a share of max loss. Evidence unit: one scored name in that band; supports = it lost.

statement: Results cluster: after a day when most scored flies lost because moves beat implied, the next day's flies do worse than average.
test: Evidence unit: one day-to-day transition after a losing day; supports = the next day also lost on balance.

statement: Names blocked for a wide ATM spread are worth a 1-contract test: patient mid limits keep enough of the mid-priced result.
test: Live round trips on names with ATM spread above 12% keep less than half of the mid-priced P/L. Evidence unit: one scored or traded name; supports = it won at mid or filled at 92%+ of mid.

statement: The no-edge gate is right: names above edge ratio 0.85 average no better than zero.
test: Evidence unit: one name blocked for no edge; supports = it lost or broke even, contradicts = it won.

note: R/I 0.70 sits on the line; fly -34% of max loss.
R/I 0.68 sits on the line; fly +11% of max loss.
R/I 0.70 sits on the line; fly +48% of max loss.
at mid: fly -19% of max loss; real fills unknown.
at mid: fly +62% of max loss; real fills unknown.
at mid: fly +48% of max loss; real fills unknown.
at mid: fly +75% of max loss; real fills unknown.
Live entry on a 16.7% ATM spread filled at 0.972 of mid; the exit is still to come.
11/04 entries (ARM, QCOM, APP, ALB) all lost; 11/05 entries (WYNN, IREN, NET, VST) all lost too.
After the 11/05 losses, 12 of 14 flies entered 11/09 won.

statement: The macro veto (a tier-1 release before the exit, or SPY moving 2% or more) blocks days that are no worse than average.
test: Evidence unit: one vetoed day with at least 4 scored flies; supports = they won on balance, contradicts = they lost on balance.

note: 11/09 was vetoed (CPI the next morning, SPY +2.49%); 12 of 14 flies entered that day won.

statement: The stock-specific-news veto can be lifted when the event is public, dated and already in the option prices, at 1 contract.
test: Evidence unit: one name traded or scored under such a waiver; supports = the fly did no worse than the average scored fly, contradicts = it lost more than half its max loss.

statement: After every journal write and before every commit, run `PYTHONPATH=src python -m vantage_trader.earnings selfcheck`; fix any failed check before committing.
test: A drift between the journal, positions file and metrics reaches a commit.

note: Would have flagged the mis-journaled RGTI trim at once (journal open quantity vs positions file).
Situational, not a daily check. Kept as step 7 of the v1.2.1 entry procedure in RULES_CHANGELOG.

statement: For every earnings fly: the evening after the report write a P/L projection (`project`); the next morning record actuals at the open and at the exit and split the error with `project-check`. Log both in state/earnings/projections.jsonl.
test: An earnings fly is closed without a scored projection.
